title: Maximize Spanning Tree Stability with Upgrades
summary: Given an integer n representing n nodes numbered from 0 to n-1 and a list of edges where each edge is defined as edges[i] = [u_i, v_i, s_i, m_i] : - u_i and v_i indicate an undirected edge between nodes u_i and v_i .
statement: Given an integer n representing n nodes numbered from 0 to n-1 and a list of edges where each edge is defined as edges[i] = [u_i, v_i, s_i, m_i] : - u_i and v_i indicate an undirected edge between nodes u_i and v_i . - s_i is the strength of the edge. - m_i is an integer (0 or 1). If m_i = 1 , the edge must be included in the spanning tree and cannot be upgraded. You are also given an integer k , which is the maximum number of upgrades you can perform. Each upgrade doubles the strength of an eligible edge (where m_i = 0 ), and each eligible edge can be upgraded at most once. The stability of a spanning tree is defined as the minimum strength score among all edges included in it. Determine the maximum possible stability of any valid spanning tree. If it is impossible to connect all nodes, return -1.
constraints: Mandatory edges must appear and cannot be upgraded.
Optional edges may be doubled once using at most k upgrades.
hints: Threshold feasibility separates required, free, and upgraded edges.
Add mandatory edges, then strong free edges, then qualifying upgraded edges.
The predicate is monotone and free-first minimizes upgrades.
editorial: The predicate is monotone and free-first minimizes upgrades.

tests.explanation: The mandatory strength-two edge caps stability at two.
Upgrading strengths four and three yields stability six.
